subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw add a caller-visible run-progress observation surface for peer sessions_send runs, and should the permanent API be sessions_subscribe/agent.events or a sessions_send progress option?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but API shape, authorization, redaction, replay retention, and channel delivery semantics are product/security choices that source inspection cannot safely decide.

options.title: Add sessions_subscribe plus agent.events
options.body: Create a separate read-only progress observation path with explicit permission checks, bounded per-run replay, event filters, and focused tests for session isolation.

options.title: Add an opt-in sessions_send progress mode
options.body: Keep a single tool surface but require a clear request/response contract for progress chunks and compatibility with ordinary sessions_send callers.

options.title: Defer to structured process events
options.body: Fold this into the broader process-event design in #52826, accepting that sessions_send progress remains unavailable until that architecture lands.

recommendation.title: Add sessions_subscribe plus agent.events
recommendation.body: Create a separate read-only progress observation path with explicit permission checks, bounded per-run replay, event filters, and focused tests for session isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated work on sessions_send, A2A behavior, ACP/session handling, and run-wait helpers that this API would touch.
